clue.text: Check safe's cover again

blocks.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
sure in the sense of secure, as in 'a sure footing'

explanation.surface: Someone tells a householder to look at whether the safe is still covered by the policy again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check safe's' reads like an instruction about a strongbox; the apostrophe-s is just 'has' joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinsure is to take out insurance once more, providing fresh protection against loss.

clue.text: Bring back spun fabric in right length

indicators.note: something spun round is turned to face the other way, so the fabric's word runs backwards
the turned fabric sits inside the letters for right and length

blocks.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right
lace is a delicate openwork fabric
L is the usual abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: A tailor is asked to return some spun cloth cut to the correct length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spun fabric' sounds like yarn or thread, but spun only tells you to turn the fabric word round.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall is to summon back or order the return of something, such as a faulty product.

clue.text: In uprising, declare billionaires opposed to freedom

indicators.note: 'in' says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows
in a down clue, rising up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words, from the end of declare to the start of billionaires

explanation.surface: A political call to denounce the super-rich during a revolt as enemies of liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uprising' suggests a revolution, which suits the anti-billionaire surface, but here it just turns the hidden letters upside down in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiberal views restrict personal liberties and resist tolerance, so they are hostile to freedom.

clue.text: Able seaman's beginning to get wasted

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of seaman
wasted is slang for killed, as in a gangster film

explanation.surface: A sailor's first steps towards getting thoroughly drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Able seaman' is a naval rank, which hides that 'Able' alone is the definition; 'wasted' looks like drunk but means murdered.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilled has the expertise or competence to do a task well, so is capable.

clue.text: Thick-skinned type articulated sarcastic denial

indicators.note: articulated means spoken out, so the words are to be judged by their sound

blocks.note: a drawled 'Ri-ight... no' is a sarcastic way of refusing something, said quickly with the T swallowed

explanation.surface: An insensitive person mouths a sneering refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick-skinned type' reads as an unfeeling person, but it is the animal with a famously tough hide.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros has an armour-like hide, making it literally a heavy-hided beast.

clue.text: One dotting i, crossing t with style

indicators.note: a word crossing a letter lies across it, so the letter ends up within that word

blocks.note: a style is a title or form of address, as in 'styled Lord'
the letter t as written

explanation.surface: Handwriting advice: dot your i's and cross your t's with a flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes 'dot the i's and cross the t's'; the dot over a lower-case i has its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: A tittle is the small diacritic mark, such as the point placed above a lower-case letter i or j.

clue.text: Depth marker is near middle of hot tub

indicators.note: the middle of a three-letter word is its central letter alone

blocks.note: taken as written
the centre letter of hot
a bath is a tub for bathing

explanation.surface: A gauge for water depth stands next to the centre of a hot tub.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobath is a line on a chart joining points of equal water depth, used to show the seabed's contours.

clue.text: Upset at repetitive strain injury in ankle bones

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the short word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
RSI is the usual initialism for repetitive strain injury

explanation.surface: A worker distressed at a typing injury that has spread to their ankles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like an emotion, but it only flips the little word at.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsal bones form the rear part of the foot, joining the leg at the joint above the heel.

clue.text: Boost source of electric current throttled by Greens misguidedly

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter
something misguided has gone astray, so these letters are led into a new order
something throttled is gripped round the neck, so it ends up enclosed

blocks.note: the opening letter of electric
taken as written
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Environmental campaigners clumsily choke off a supply of electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of electric stands at the front; the current symbol then goes inside the rearranged Greens.
explanation.definitionFit: To energise is to give vitality or power to something, so it means to invigorate.

clue.text: Deduced most of info was wrong

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written; its last letter goes
to have erred is to have been wrong

explanation.surface: A detective works out that the bulk of the information was false.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to reach a conclusion by reasoning from evidence, the past tense matching worked out.

clue.text: Way in which we're sure to have an impact?

definitions.text: Way in which we're sure to have an impact?

blocks.clueFragment: Way in which we're sure to have an impact?
blocks.note: surface reading: a method guaranteed to make an impression or be influential

blocks.clueFragment: Way in which we're sure to have an impact?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a route on which two moving things will certainly crash into each other

explanation.surface: A campaigner asks how to be sure of making a difference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impact' is taken figuratively in the surface, but literally means a crash; 'way' is a path or trajectory.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a trajectory that, if unchanged, will end in a crash with another object.

clue.text: Lance corporal ultimately introduced by dog tag

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the closing letters of the two words are kept

blocks.note: a lab is a Labrador retriever
the final letters of Lance and of corporal

explanation.surface: A soldier is finally fitted with a dog tag for identification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lance corporal' looks like a single rank to abbreviate, but each word gives its own last letter. 'Introduced by' puts the dog first.
explanation.definitionFit: A label is a small attached ticket identifying something, the same as an identifying tag.

clue.text: Working out at first gym class

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: the opening letter of out
PE, physical education, is the school subject often called gym
a rating is a class or grade, as in a film's age rating

explanation.surface: Someone working out, starting with a gym class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working out' looks like a phrase, but 'Working' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is operating is running and functioning, i.e. in action.

clue.text: One making play has to nudge Romeo after botched cue

indicators.note: a botched job is messed up, so the letters of the short word are jumbled

blocks.note: to prod is to nudge or poke
taken as written, then rearranged
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A theatre producer has to prompt the actor playing Romeo after he misses his cue.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo is a theatrical name here, which helps hide that he is just the letter R; 'after' puts him at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A producer is the person who stages and finances a show, so is responsible for mounting a theatrical work.

clue.text: Recording caught asset with the shot of heroin

indicators.note: to be shot of something is to be rid of it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written
taken as written, then losing a letter
H is slang for heroin; this letter is the one removed

explanation.surface: Someone was caught on tape with valuables and a shot of heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot of heroin' paints a drug fix, but 'shot of' means rid of, so the word the loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette is a tape cartridge holding recorded sound, so it is a recording medium.

clue.text: Somewhere on campus, does drag for audience

indicators.note: something put on for an audience is heard rather than read, so go by the sound

blocks.note: hauls means drags along, and in British speech it sounds like the answer

explanation.surface: A university venue puts on drag shows for an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does drag' suggests performing in drag; read it as a verb, it means pulls. Halls of residence are student accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: Halls, short for halls of residence, are the student accommodation blocks found at a university.

clue.text: Huge monster returning? No thanks, I've left!

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the string of words is read backwards

blocks.note: nah is a casual no
ta is British informal for thanks
taken as written, without the apostrophe
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone flees a returning monster, shouting that they want no part of it and are off.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation looks like the definition's punchline, but every word of it feeds the reversed string.
explanation.definitionFit: Leviathan is the biblical sea beast, and the word now denotes anything enormous and powerful.

clue.text: Copper tucked into fresh scampi and pepper

indicators.note: fresh suggests something made anew, so the seafood's letters are remade in another order
something tucked into a thing is pushed inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman tucks into a plate of fresh scampi with pepper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer eating, but it is the chemical element. Scampi are breaded fried prawns.
explanation.definitionFit: Capsicum is the botanical genus of sweet and chilli peppers, and the usual name for a bell pepper in some countries.

clue.text: Maps mineral area to the west

definitions.note: a plural noun for a singular answer: the answer is a book of maps

indicators.note: in an across entry, heading west means running right to left, so the letters go backwards

blocks.note: salt is a common mineral
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A geologist charts mineral deposits in a region to the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maps' looks like a verb, but it is the definition as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound collection of charts of the world or a region.

clue.text: Attacked and brought back spoils by sea

indicators.note: something brought back returns along its path, so the word reads in the opposite direction

blocks.note: food that spoils rots
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: Raiders attacked and carried off plunder by ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoils' looks like loot, which suits the pirate picture, but it is a verb meaning goes bad.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm a position is to assault it violently, so the past tense matches made an assault on.

clue.text: Drug's bearing on case

blocks.note: SE, south-east, is a compass bearing
the dative is a grammatical case

explanation.surface: A medicine has an effect on a patient's condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing on case' reads like relevance to a lawsuit or patient; it is a compass direction then a grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedative is a calming medicine that induces sleep or reduces anxiety.

clue.text: Having bequests start from these belongings

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of these
an estate is everything a person owns, especially at death

explanation.surface: Someone leaving gifts in a will, beginning with these possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: A person dying testate has left a valid will, so their legacies are set out in writing.

clue.text: Left poorly after eating yellow bit of broccoli

indicators.note: something poorly is out of sorts, so the letters are disordered
having eaten something, a word holds it inside

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone feels unwell after eating a yellowing piece of broccoli.
explanation.walkthrough: Or is the heraldic word for gold, standing for yellow here.
explanation.definitionFit: A floret is one of the small flowering heads that make up a head of broccoli or cauliflower.

clue.text: Leads on sets of each period drama

indicators.note: the leads of words are their front letters, so the first letter of each is kept

blocks.note: the first letters of sets and of
a pop means each, as in 'five pounds a pop'
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Star actors working on the sets of every costume drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Period drama' is a strong phrase, but 'period' belongs to the wordplay and 'drama' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial drama on TV or radio about the lives of a group of characters.

clue.text: Cancel yearly bar crawl at centre

indicators.note: at centre picks out the single middle letter of the word before it
bar means except, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: annual means once a year
the middle letter of crawl

explanation.surface: Calling off the annual pub crawl in the town centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar crawl' reads as a pub crawl, but 'bar' means minus and 'crawl at centre' is a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare void or invalid, as with a marriage or contract, so it means revoke.

clue.text: Early barely understood slang

indicators.note: barely suggests something stripped bare, so the word loses its outer letters

blocks.note: taken as written, then stripped down to its two inner letters
to have got something is to have understood it

explanation.surface: Early dialect that was hardly comprehended.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip early of its first letter and its -ly ending, leaving AR, then add GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the jargon or private vocabulary of a particular group, such as thieves.

clue.text: Small, hard tool making holes in woollen cloth

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
an awl is a pointed tool for piercing leather or wood

explanation.surface: A small hard tool punches holes in a piece of wool fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making holes' describes the awl and is not a container signal; the pieces simply run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A shawl is a piece of fabric, often knitted from wool, worn around the shoulders.

clue.text: Filmmaker misrepresented Taichang Emperor

indicators.note: something misrepresented is shown wrongly, so the letters are presented in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written; the Taichang Emperor was a Ming ruler of China in 1620

explanation.surface: A director made a misleading film about a Chinese emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: The obscure emperor's name is there only for its fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinematographer is the director of photography who controls camera and lighting when shooting a movie.

clue.text: Combine yttrium with oxygen in air

indicators.note: in says the element's symbol goes inside the letters already assembled

blocks.note: to meld is to blend or combine
Y is the chemical symbol for yttrium
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A chemistry instruction to mix elements in the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' looks like part of the chemistry, but it is the musical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune or song, so it is the same as a musical line.

clue.text: What surfer may use, having disturbed the sea-eagle close to nest

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown out of place, so the letters of the little word are rearranged
the close of a word is its end, so its last letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the erne is the white-tailed sea eagle
the final letter of nest

explanation.surface: A wave rider disturbs a sea eagle near its nest.
explanation.walkthrough: The surfer looks like someone on a board, but is a web surfer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethernet is the standard wired networking technology for connecting computers to the internet, which web browsers rely on.
